# zlib-ng / fuzzer_example_dict

zlib-ng's own fuzz target `fuzzer_example_dict` ([source](source/fuzzer_example_dict.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over zlib-ng (zlib-ng/zlib-ng at 1579085c).

Checks 2 properties (listed below); the first, a round trip: deflateInit2 (level/windowBits/memLevel/strategy from data[0..3]) with a preset dictionary = first data[0] bytes of the input, then inflate supplying the dictionary on Z_NEED_DICT; output must memcmp-equal the input.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against zlib-ng at commit 1579085c.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- Every zlib call must return Z_OK (CHECK_ERR -> exit(1)); deflate(Z_FINISH) into 100+2*deflateBound bytes must return Z_STREAM_END; the dictionary id requested by inflate must equal the Adler-32 recorded after deflateSetDictionary ([lines 61-125](source/fuzzer_example_dict.c#L61-L125)): exit(1); confirmed in the binary.
- deflateInit2 (level/windowBits/memLevel/strategy from data[0..3]) with a preset dictionary = first data[0] bytes of the input, then inflate supplying the dictionary on Z_NEED_DICT; output must memcmp-equal the input ([lines 127-130](source/fuzzer_example_dict.c#L127-L130)): exit(1); not confirmed in the binary.

A failure of the check at lines 61-125 ends the process with a status that the halts statements below that name it exclude, so a proof of one of those statements implies it on every input it covers. No statement here proves the other check.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch zlib-ng` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzzer_example_dict.plain` | 156,864 | `d19e391bd1b1d15da0397646d4012451ff15b25d93cb7b839f50a7824fc2ecb2` |
| ubsan | `fuzzer_example_dict.ubsan` | 154,344 | `0ae71ec76d7e7a475ae7bab97922bf4edc08cd7befa46c84716d86b7e6242510` |
| asan | `fuzzer_example_dict.asan` | 826,744 | `5f412df02f240f8e9ac2ec9dbcfcdaa58e8f7496bdf0eee08dd46bf8c46a747b` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzzer_example_dict.asan-ubsan` | 801,976 | `e5b33ae2035c7a04463f70a429b8ac70a43a022a59718b1ff64801f94b9d278e` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
